article_notes: Prospective OVAH study, 34 B. rossi dogs (PCR/RLB) and 24 healthy controls. The only severity analysis is 25(OH)D against an author-built clinical severity score (Table 2). Table 2 row label appears to be a copy error (see row note). Sex, age and weight in Table 2 are covariates of 25(OH)D, not tested against severity, so not extracted. ALT, creatinine and time since last meal were tested against 25(OH)D, not against severity. Samples taken on admission; timing relative to treatment not stated.

severity_definitions.label: clinical severity score (0-12)
severity_definitions.definition: Author-built cumulative score, 1 point each for: basal cortisol > 275 nmol/L, ACTH > 20 pg/mL, T4 < 2.8 nmol/L, albumin < 20, potassium < 3.6 mmol/L, phosphate > 1.94 mmol/L, creatinine > 133 umol/L, bile acids >= 55 umol/L, glucose < 3.3 mmol/L, icterus, band cells > 10%, body temperature < 37.8 C (maximum 12). 'other' covers the endocrine, electrolyte, albumin, band-cell and hypothermia items. Observed range 0-10, median 2 (n = 34).

associations.statistic: linear model of 25(OH)D on severity score: estimate −4.09, SE 1.06, t −3.86
associations.note: In Table 2 the row is labelled 'Babesiosis (reference = healthy control)', apparently copied from Table 1; the table title and Results text say this model tests disease severity in infected dogs only, so the row is read as the severity-score coefficient (25(OH)D falls about 4.09 nmol/L per score point). Abstract and Discussion also report an inverse correlation with the clinical severity score.
